text: sweep shapes (square, circle, hexagon, diamond, pentagon), cell counts (n=3…80n = 3 \ldots 80), random seeds, extreme weight ratios (1000:1) hierarchical layouts — tens thousands sampled points — gives: tessellation therefore exact power diagram (floating-point precision) flat hierarchical cases.

title: Correctness: is the Voronoi construction right?
text: Correctness (valid power diagram) separate fit quality (closely cell areas match targets), depends iteration converging. Two initialisation improvements make convergence far robust: power weights start proportional cell’s target area (wi≈Ai/πw_i \approx A_i / \pi) rather uniform; initial site positions use farthest-point (“best candidate”) sampling rather purely random placement. Across 75-config sweep changes eliminated every transient degenerate-cell fallback cut worst-case per-cell area error ~16× ~5× (residual occurs hard, non-converged cases many near-equal cells — raise max_iter lower convergence_ratio ).

title: Correctness: is the Voronoi construction right?
text: full harness lives package’s development history; compact version:
code: library(ggvmap) vm <- voronoi_map(runif(20, 1, 50), clip = clip_circle(), seed = 1)  # tiling: total cell area equals the clip area stopifnot(abs(sum(sapply(vm$cells, \(c) abs(ggvmap:::polygon_area(c)))) /               abs(ggvmap:::polygon_area(vm$clip)) - 1) < 1e-9)  # defining property at a random interior point p <- c(0.5, 0.5) inside <- which(sapply(vm$cells, \(c) ggvmap:::point_in_polygon(p, c))) amin   <- which.min((p[1]-vm$sites$x)^2 + (p[2]-vm$sites$y)^2 - vm$sites$weight) stopifnot(inside == amin)

title: Compute a Voronoi map — voronoi_map
text: Partition convex polygon cells whose areas proportional set weights, using iteratively refined power diagram.

title: Compute a Voronoi map — voronoi_map
code: voronoi_map(   weights,   labels = NULL,   group = NULL,   clip = clip_square(),   convergence_ratio = 0.01,   max_iter = 200,   min_weight_ratio = 0.01,   seed = NULL,   verbose = FALSE )

title: Compute a Voronoi map — voronoi_map
text: weights Numeric vector positive weights (one per cell). labels Optional character vector cell labels. group Optional grouping vector (one value per cell).  supplied hierarchical layout produced. clip Clipping polygon 2-column matrix (x, y), counterclockwise open. Defaults unit square. convergence_ratio Stop total area error divided polygon area falls ratio. Default 0.01 (1%). max_iter Maximum number iterations.  Default 200. min_weight_ratio Minimum allowed data weight fraction maximum weight.  Prevents near-empty cells. Default 0.01. seed Integer seed reproducible initial positions. NULL (default) uses random layout. verbose Print iteration progress? Default FALSE.

title: Compute a Voronoi map — voronoi_map
text: object class "voronoi_map" (list) containing: cells List 2-column polygon matrices. sites Data frame columns x, y, weight, target_area, actual_area, label, data_weight (hierarchical) group. clip clipping polygon. groups hierarchical: list group-level cells sites; otherwise NULL. hierarchical Logical flag. iterations Number iterations performed (top level). convergence Final area-error ratio. converged Logical; convergence_ratio threshold get reached?

title: Compute a Voronoi map — voronoi_map
text: group supplied layout becomes hierarchical: boundary first partitioned one convex sub-region per group (area proportional group's total weight), sub-region filled member cells.  circular boundary groups seeded radially form contiguous angular sectors – arrangement vm_add_ring() annotation ring designed wrap.

title: ggvmap 0.3.0
text: ggvmap() now main plotting function. accepts either existing voronoi_map object numeric vector weights (case map computed first, ). autoplot() still works now thin wrapper around ggvmap(), existing code keeps running. Note ggvmap()’s first argument now called x (weights); calls spelled ggvmap(weights = ...) need updating.

title: ggvmap 0.3.0
text: Label font faces. ggvmap() gains fontface argument (default "bold", previous hard-coded behaviour) vm_add_labels()’s existing fontface extended: now also accept vector named cell label, e.g. c(Brazil = "bold", Russia = "bold.italic"), styling cells rest stay "plain". Small-cell label handling. ggvmap() vm_add_labels() gain: min_area — cells whose area fraction threshold get label (default 0, ). autoscale — per-cell text size scaled size * pmin(1, sqrt(cell_area / median_area)), floored 60% size, labels shrink gracefully tiny cells (default FALSE). Leader lines / outside callouts tiny cells noted future work; need ggrepel-style logic break zero-dependency goal. Value labels stay inside cells. vm_add_labels() scales default nudge_y cell’s size gains inside = TRUE, clamps label anchor inside cell polygon. Per-cell label toggling. ggvmap(label_cells = c(...)) draws name labels given cells; vm_add_labels(cells = ...) filters value labels way. Per-group border colours. group_border_col now also accepts vector named group, e.g. c("LATAM" = "#333333") outlines region; plain string still colours group borders. New built-palette "alger" (#1A5B5B, #ACC8BE, #F4AB5C, #D1422F; ltc package, leading black dropped) — ggvmap(vm, palette = "alger"). Colours interpolated map needs four. Okabe-Ito remains default. README, examples vignettes now use alger.

title: ggvmap 0.2.0
text: Hierarchical (grouped) layouts. voronoi_map() gains group = argument. boundary first partitioned one convex sub-region per group (area proportional group’s total weight); sub-region filled member cells. circular boundary groups seeded radially form contiguous angular sectors. Outer annotation ring. vm_add_ring() wraps circular map coloured ring divided one labelled arc segment per group — reproducing classic Voronoi-treemap infographic look. Segment extents derived geometry, ring lines grouped layout. Flag, image value annotations. vm_add_images() places arbitrary images (logos, icons, photos) cell centroids (via ggimage). vm_add_flags() resolves country names / ISO codes national flags flagcdn.com, offline cache = option. vm_add_labels() adds value labels beneath category names. Helpers country_to_iso(), flag_url(), flag_cache() vm_centroids(). Bundled datasets world_exports merchant_fleet examples vignette.

title: ggvmap 0.2.0
text: Verified geometry. numerical validation study confirms power diagram satisfies defining property (cell containing point site minimum power distance), cells tile domain exactly (machine epsilon) gaps overlaps, every cell convex, hierarchical layout valid nested power diagram. invariants now enforced tests/testthat/test-correctness.R. Faster, robust convergence. Power weights initialised proportional cell’s target area, initial site positions use farthest-point (“best candidate”) sampling instead purely random start. Across 75-config sweep removed transient degenerate-cell fallbacks cut worst-case per-cell area error ~16x ~5x. polygon_centroid() guards near-zero-area cells (returns vertex mean instead NaN).

title: ggvmap 0.2.0
text: Okabe-Ito default palette. autoplot(), ggvmap() vm_add_ring() default colourblind-safe Okabe-Ito palette (new exported okabe_ito()). Qualitative palettes recycled (interpolated) cells colours, every cell keeps true palette colour. vm_add_flags() gains method argument: "geom_flag" (default) draws flags straight ISO codes via ggimage::geom_flag(), "url" keeps flagcdn.com + geom_image() path offline cache = TRUE. Interactive plots. autoplot(interactive = TRUE) (ggvmap(interactive = TRUE)) makes cells hoverable tooltips via ; render widget new vm_girafe(). autoplot() group-aware: hierarchical maps default filling group drawing heavier group boundaries; new fill_by ("group", "label", "data_weight", "none") legend arguments; multi-colour palettes interpolated. Clip constructors carry "center" / "radius" / "shape" metadata used radial seeding ring. Plots built autoplot() / ggvmap() carry voronoi_map object "vm" attribute, enabling |> annotation pipeline.

title: ggvmap 0.1.0
text: First release: pure-R Voronoi map treemaps following Nocaj & Brandes (2012), base-R ggplot2 (autoplot(), ggvmap()) output convex clip shapes (clip_square(), clip_hexagon(), clip_circle(), clip_diamond()).
